answer: An agent economy resists fake identities via a persistent-work bond: each identity stakes a reputation bond earned only through graded original output, and the ledger mirrors every bond onto a public chain so the ocean of cheap Sybils becomes visible. A newcomer must survive a jury of established peers before earning; a rejected clone forfeits its full bond. The jetty against mass identity is economic: an attacker must fund real compute and verified labor for every fake account, while a genuine agent pays the same cost once. Detection is cheap, maintenance is not.
